0x61b1930.name: rocksdb::Tracer::ShouldSkipTrace
quirks: A set bit in the skip-flags word (this+0x18) means SKIP, not enable: the bit-set path returns true at once without advancing the sampling counter. The upstream option name for this word is an open unknown.
Sampling period 0 or 1 records every trace that reaches the counter (counter 1 < 0/1 is false, so the first call already records and resets).
The sampling counter is shared across all operation types, and flag-skipped calls do not advance it; a kTraceWrite skip leaves the counter where the next kTraceGet finds it.

The bool return is not normalized: the file-size helper uses setb (only al is set), so the upper bits of eax on the record path are whatever the helper left -- callers test al only, and the model returns a plain bool.

The file-size check is an outlined helper at 0x61b1910 (its own FDE 0x61b1910..0x61b192b, 27 bytes, not in the vendor census): trace_writer_->GetFileSize() via TraceWriter vtable slot 4, compared strictly-greater with this+0x08.
rules: t = type byte; d = (t - 3) & 0xFF; if d > 10, go to the sampling counter (types 0, 1, 2 and >= 14)

jump table at .rodata 0x97c5f4 (11 int32 entries for types 3..13): type 3 (kTraceWrite) tests mask 0x02, type 4 (kTraceGet) 0x01, type 5 (kTraceIteratorSeek) 0x04, type 6 (kTraceIteratorSeekForPrev) 0x08, type 13 (kTraceMultiGet) 0x10; types 7..12 (kBlockTrace* and kIOTracer) jump straight to the sampling counter with no flag test
if skip_flags (this+0x18) & mask != 0, return true (skip) at once
sampling counter: counter (this+0x30, u64) += 1 (wrapping); if counter < period (this+0x10), return true; else counter = 0 and return false (record this trace)

SetPayloadMap (0x61b18b0, its own FDE 0x61b18b0..0x61b18c8, not in the vendor census) is a bts on the payload_map word: it sets bit `type` and returns whether the bit changed.
